courses.description: Fundamental concepts in numerical linear algebra. Fundamental matrix decompositions: LU, Cholesky, QR, Eigen, Schur, Jordan, SVD; how to compute them. Solution of large linear systems via iterative methods (Lanczos, Arnoldi, CG, GMRES). Stability of algorithms and conditioning of mathematical problems. Finite precision arithmetic and roundoff issues. Additional topics may include randomized methods for computing SVD/QR and solution of Lyapunov/Riccati equations for high-dimensional systems.
courses.prereqText: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Numerical Differential Equations
courses.description: Finite difference approximation. Initial value ODEs: explicit, implicit, accuracy, stability, convergence, Runge-Kutta and multipoint methods, stiff systems. Boundary value ODEs: shooting and equilibrium method. PDEs: stability and accuracy. Hyperbolic PDEs: central and upwinding methods, linear advection, Burgers equation. Parabolic PDEs: convection-diffusion equation, multidimensional problems. Elliptic PDEs: direct solution, iterative solution, multigrid method. Fourier spectral method.
courses.prereqText: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Numerical methods in fluid dynamics and convective transport processes. Numerical solution of the Euler and Navier-Stokes equation. Additional topics will vary according to instructor. Examples include eigenvalue problems in hydrodynamic stability, vortex methods, spectral and panel methods.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Design and Mechanics in Computer Technology
courses.description: Design and mechanics problems inherent in computer peripherals such as disk files, tape drives, and printers. Formulation and solution of problems involving mechanics, fluid mechanics, and materials; Reynolds equation, slider bearings; friction and wear; actuator design, impact printing; silicon fluid jets.
courses.prereqText: consent of instructor. (Not offered every year.)

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Computer-Aided Design and Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to 2-D and 3-D computer-aided design. Design problems may include ball bearing kinematics, Weibull statistics, nonrepeatable spindle run-out, four bar linkages, beam deflection and vibration, design of magnetic head suspension, hydrodynamic theory of lubrication, air bearings, heat transfer, optical servo, design of ink jet print head.
courses.prereqText: consent of instructor. (Not offered every year.)

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Flow Control
courses.description: Intersection of control theory and fluid mechanics. Applications: transition delay, turbulence mitigation, noise reduction, weather forecasting, shape optimization, and UAV’s (perching). Tractable feedback (Riccati-based) formulations via parallel and parabolic flow assumptions. Regularization of variational (adjoint-based) formulations for MPC and MHE. EnKF and EnVE approaches for forecasting.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Mathematics
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SIO 203A.) Review of exact methods for ordinary differential equations. Expansions about regular and irregular singular points, eigenfunction methods for ordinary differential equations, special functions, Fourier series and integral transforms, linear algebra.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Mathematics II
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SIO 203B.) Partial differential equations: characteristics, similarity solutions, Green’s functions, images, wave equation, diffusion equation, Laplace’s equation. Applications to continuum mechanics, potential fields, and transport phenomena such as diffusion, linear and nonlinear waves, Burger’s equation, shocks, and other topics. Other topics according to the interests of the instructor.
courses.prereqText: MAE 294A or SIO 203A or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Mathematics III
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SIO 203C.) Perturbation theory, asymptotic methods and asymptotic expansions. Approximate methods for linear and nonlinear differential equations, such as WKB, the method of multiple scales and boundary layer theory.
courses.prereqText: MAE 294B or SIO 203B or SIO 215B or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Field Study
courses.description: Provides field study in industry with faculty supervision. Analysis and problem solving using real world applications.
courses.prereqText: consent of adviser and department; 3.0 GPA.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem as arranged by a designated faculty member. Must be taken for a letter grade only.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in regular department curriculum, by special arrangement with a faculty member.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students engaged in research and writing theses. (S/U grades only.)
